results.summary_before: This is a silicon implementation of an Enigma I cipher machine with a limited three-wire plugboard and a 52-bit key length. It takes 5-bit data and 3-bit command inputs, returns data on the bidirectional pins with a ready signal, and drives the on-board 7-segment display. No external hardware is needed because it uses the PCB's built-in display. The design is notable for implementing a historical rotor cipher machine in Amaranth on a single tile.
results.summary: This is a RISC-V based system that boots by accessing an SPI flash over the SPI bus, configuring it in XIP mode and executing instructions from it. It exposes four GPIO pins that can be used to output data, for example as a bitbanged UART. The design is written in Verilog and targets a 2x2 tile area. Testing uses a testbench containing an SPI flash model preloaded with a program in Verilog Hex format, and the project can be run locally with FuseSoC.
